clauses.current_legal_basis: The order's own held text read with the bounded searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog: 5 U.S.C. 5948 note (U.S. Code release point 119-121) prints the order as current text; 5 U.S.C. 5948 is in force with no sunset; 5 CFR part 595 (eCFR point-in-time 2026-10-14) cites E.O. 12109 in its authority; no held later instrument amends or revokes the designation.
clauses.reason: Section 1-101 designates and empowers the Director of OPM, in consultation with the Director of OMB, to exercise the President's authority under 5 U.S.C. 5948 to prescribe regulations, criteria and conditions for physicians' comparability allowances. It has no own-terms end and no held instrument ends or amends it; 5 U.S.C. 5948 remains in force and 5 CFR part 595 relies on the order, so it is operative on 2026-10-14.

Section 1-102 says that until the Office of Personnel Management is established (on or before January 1, 1979), pursuant to Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1978, the Civil Service Commission shall exercise the authority delegated under the order. The condition occurred on January 1, 1979: the held text of EO 12107, section 1-101, makes the establishment of OPM under the Reorganization Plan effective on that date, and 1-102's own wording sets that date as the latest. The actor is the order itself (own terms); the first end is the date OPM came into existence, January 1, 1979, so the Civil Service Commission's exercise ended then.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 12109 of December 28, 1978 (44 FR 1067), Federal Physicians Comparability Allowance, has two numbered sections in the held Federal Register text. Section 1-101 designates and empowers the Director of the Office of Personnel Management, in consultation with the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, to exercise the President's authority under 5 U.S.C. 5948 to prescribe regulations, criteria and conditions for comparability allowances for certain Federal physicians. Section 1-102 provides that until OPM is established (on or before January 1, 1979) under Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1978 the Civil Service Commission exercises that authority. The packet's single whole clause covered both, so I corrected the inventory into two clauses with absolute character spans in the held original text: 1-101 operative, 1-102 terminated by its own terms. The held text of EO 12107 (jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_12107.txt, section 1-101) states that the establishment of OPM under Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1978 is effective January 1, 1979; that is the date on which the until-OPM-is-established condition occurred and the transitional command to the Civil Service Commission ended, by the order's own terms. EO 12107 does not amend EO 12109 and is cited only as the source of the date. Search of held texts for the number EO 12109 finds only the order and 5 CFR part 595 (authority citation); the OFR catalog record has no disposition note; the bounded searches report no machine hit that ends or amends the order. The Office of the Law Revision Counsel U.S. Code release point 119-121 (edition current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-14 are not reflected in that edition) prints the order as a note and records no ending statement, and the packet holds no source showing a later statute that affects it. 5 U.S.C. 5948 note prints the order's text as current, including section 1-102 as historical text. The held text of 5 U.S.C. 5948 (jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t5-s5948.txt) is in the Code with no sunset provision, and the eCFR search (point-in-time as of 2026-10-14) finds 5 CFR part 595 (physicians' comparability allowances), whose authority citation names E.O. 12109. Section 1-101 is therefore operative as of 2026-10-14.

savings.reason: Section 1-102 ended on January 1, 1979 when OPM was established; it was a transitional allocation of the same delegated authority to the Civil Service Commission, and no action under it needs saving beyond what the continuing delegation in 1-101 and 5 CFR part 595 already govern. No claim is made that any residual duty under 1-102 survives.
